issues.legal_issue: Land on which a building is under construction remains rateable and may be assessed as vacant land until a part of the construction is legally and actually capable of occupation.
material_facts: The owner held a large plot, some of which was vacant and some of which was covered by an incomplete building under construction.
The assessor valued the construction area as land and assessed its hypothetical annual rental value.
There was no material showing that any part of the building was complete or legally and actually capable of occupation.
The High Court held that the construction area was not rateable while construction continued, applying the doctrine of sterility.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed. The construction area did not cease to be rateable merely because a building was being erected on it; as no part was shown to be capable of occupation, the whole land was to be valued as vacant land and the matter was remitted for reassessment.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(r) and 154(1) of the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, land includes land being built upon, and rateable value is directed to the annual letting value. Land under construction remains rateable; until the building or a part of it is legally and actually capable of occupation, it may be treated as vacant land. The English doctrine of sterility did not apply because the statutory basis of rating in India was not confined to beneficial occupation or income actually earned. The Court relied on Corporation of Calcutta v. S.M. Padma Debi, Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad, Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Royal Western India Turf Club, Motichand Hirachand v. Bombay Municipal Corporation, and other Indian rating decisions; it distinguished the English authorities applying sterility.

predicates.municipal_rating_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the rating assessment of land by a municipal authority.
predicates.land_is_under_construction: A building is being erected on the land being assessed.
predicates.no_part_is_legally_and_actually_occupiab: No completed part of the construction is both legally and actually capable of occupation.

issues.definition: When a municipal rating appeal concerns land under construction and no part is legally and actually occupiable, the construction land is assessed as vacant land.
